anomalies.observed: In the Capacitive Touch Button (TSC) block on the root sheet (PCB.kicad_sch, pages 1/2), the two net labels NET0003 (MCU U3 pin 57 = PB5) and NET0008 (MCU U3 pin 59 = PB7) both terminate on the same node, which also carries the top plate of C25 (22 nF) and the left terminal of R9 (1 k). Thus PB5 and PB7, the sampling capacitor and the series resistor are all merged into a single net, and the electrode (A1 'BTN') hangs off R9's right terminal from that merged node.
anomalies.expected: The specification keeps these as two separate nets: 'TSC_G2_IO2: U2 pin 57 (PB5) — R8 (1 kΩ series resistor) — A2 pin BTN' and 'TSC_G2_IO4: U2 pin 59 (PB7) — C14 (22 nF to GND)'. PB7 must connect only to the sampling capacitor (C25) to GND, and PB5 must connect only through the series resistor (R9) to the BTN electrode; the sampling-cap node and the electrode-drive node must not be joined.

evidence.quote: Capacitive Touch Button (TSC): NET0008 and NET0003 both wired into the left terminal of R9, which is also tied to C25 (22n) top (root sheet, pages 1-2)
TSC_G2_IO2: U2 pin 57 (PB5) — R8 (1 kΩ series resistor) — A2 pin "BTN" ... TSC_G2_IO4: U2 pin 59 (PB7) — C14 (22 nF to GND) — this is the TSC sampling capacitor for the group

anomalies.impact: The STM32 Touch Sensing Controller's sampling-capacitor pin (PB7) and the electrode-drive pin (PB5) are shorted together and share the external Cx and the series Rs. This violates ST's TSC topology, so the capacitive touch button will not sense correctly (the electrode is not driven from its own channel and the sampling cap is placed on the wrong pin), effectively disabling the touch input.
